final_report.summary: Successfully built a complete Natural Language Hypothesis Interface for AtlasLab across 2 cycles. Cycle 1 established the full 6-stage scientific investigation pipeline (Formulation → Derivation → Simulation → Analysis → Integration → Synthesis) with symbolic math (SymPy), numerical computation (NumPy/SciPy), dimensional analysis, knowledge base (SQLite), equation matching, consistency checking, and a Rich CLI. Cycle 2 added the NL translation layer: a 'front door' (translator.py) that converts plain English hypotheses to validated YAML via LLM, and a 'back door' (interpreter.py) that converts raw investigation results into human-readable Markdown reports. The system supports both Claude Sonnet and Ollama (local llama3.1:8b) as LLM backends with automatic fallback. A FastAPI web server with SSE streaming, a Bootstrap 5 dark-themed dashboard with NL input, progress tracking, and 'Dig Deeper' iteration, and a CLI `investigate-nl` command complete the interface. 152/152 tests pass including E2E validation with real LLM calls through Ollama.
key_achievements: Complete 6-stage scientific investigation pipeline (Formulation → Derivation → Simulation → Analysis → Integration → Synthesis)
NL front door: Plain English → validated YAML hypothesis via LLM with 3-retry validation loop
NL back door: Raw investigation results → structured Markdown report via LLM
Dual LLM support: Claude Sonnet (cloud) + Ollama llama3.1:8b (local) with automatic fallback
SSE streaming for real-time progress during NL investigation
Dig Deeper iteration: modify existing hypothesis with follow-up questions and get comparison reports
CLI NL mode: `atlaslab investigate-nl` with --show-yaml and --provider flags
Dark-themed Bootstrap 5 dashboard with NL input, progress streaming, YAML toggle, and bento grid analytics
152/152 tests passing including E2E with real LLM (Ollama)
Robust math engines: SymPy with 30s timeout guards, NumPy/SciPy numerical computation, dimensional analysis
Knowledge base with SQLite persistence, equation matching, and consistency checking
10+ hypothesis YAML files including adversarial test cases that validate error detection
challenges_overcome: SymPy timeout issues on complex symbolic operations - solved with 30s signal-based timeout guards
LLM YAML generation quality - solved with 3-retry validation loop and detailed schema prompts
Ollama local model YAML quality lower than Claude - mitigated with stronger prompt engineering and validation
SSE streaming with FastAPI required careful error handling and AbortController integration
Dimensional analysis bracket parsing edge cases - multiple rounds of hardening
canonical_form() infinite recursion on certain SymPy expressions - fixed with try/except fallback
NumPy floating point warnings during edge case computations - fixed with np.errstate context managers
lessons_learned: Validation-retry loops are essential when using LLMs for structured output generation - raw LLM output is unreliable
Ollama with smaller models (8b) can substitute for cloud APIs in development/testing but quality degrades on complex tasks
SSE streaming provides much better UX than polling for long-running scientific computations
Adversarial test hypotheses (dimensionally inconsistent, physically impossible) are invaluable for validating error detection
SymPy operations MUST have timeout guards - certain expressions cause hangs without them
Modular monolithic architecture paid off: adding the NL layer required no changes to the core pipeline
Screenshot-based UI verification catches issues that API-level testing misses (rendering, layout, JS errors)
